critique:
refused
  The three reported failures all occurred at the first execution decision, where the goal required reproducing the visible demonstration and the carried memory was empty. The policy selected a rightward clockwise move for a demonstration beginning with a larger-x, image-lower traversal; selected a rightward clockwise move for one beginning with a smaller-x, image-upper traversal; and selected a rightward counterclockwise move for one beginning with a larger-x, image-upper traversal. The correct initial commands were respectively C, D, and A. The annotated full routes were respectively ["C","C"], ["D","D","B"], and ["A","C","A","B","D"]. None of the failure reports identified missing information or an unclear rule. The existing instructions already explicitly map destination x to robot handedness, classify the arc relative to the wrist-endpoint baseline, initialize the full route from the demonstration, and select its first letter without removing it at initialization. These observations therefore do not establish a SUFFICIENCY or NECESSITY defect in the memory field or a missing subgoal transition rule. No additional memory, changed annotation, or episode-specific exception is warranted; the reported choices contradict rules already present.
